extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants (AFs and LAFs), GHG emissions attestation providers, auditors/accountants, and securities compliance lawyers
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation of SEC final rules (Regulation S‑K Items 1505–1506) governing third‑party attestation/assurance of Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and related registrant disclosures. Includes required report content, phase‑in, provider qualifications/oversight disclosure, and change/disagreement reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards due‑process / consensus development
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards that follow a multi‑stakeholder consensus process with opportunities for public comment align with the Commission's due process requirement for 'sufficiently developed' standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ISO follows a consensus process and provides public comment opportunities; that alignment supports treating ISO standards as meeting the due process requirement in the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widely used standard criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard meets the 'widely used' criterion when it is frequently relied upon in real‑world assurance engagements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example evidence: ISO 14064‑3 was used in 196 of 346 voluntary GHG assurance engagements in a cited study. Frequency of use supports that a standard is 'widely used' under the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible approach to acceptable standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will take a flexible, principles‑based approach and will not prescribe a single required standard or an exhaustive list of acceptable standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although multiple suitable standards may exist (and new ones may develop), registrants and attestation providers should use standards that satisfy the final rules' requirements. The Commission considered but rejected requiring one particular standard or listing acceptable standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation report must follow the attestation standard's form and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1506(c) requires the form and content of the GHG emissions attestation report to follow the requirements set forth by the attestation standard(s) used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules do not prescribe minimum report requirements; instead, the report should conform to the chosen prevailing attestation standard(s). This approach is principles‑based; the Commission expects prevailing standards will generally include the common elements of current assurance reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include common assurance elements when standard lacks them
rubrics_metrics.description: If a particular attestation standard does not include elements sufficiently similar to those commonly included in assurance reports, the GHG emissions attestation provider should consider including such information in its attestation report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation is to facilitate investors' understanding of the nature and scope of the engagement if the chosen standard omits commonly expected elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective application and phased‑in coverage of historical periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules apply prospectively with historical period disclosure phasing in over time: in the first year a registrant (AF or LAF) is required to provide an attestation report, the report need only cover Scope 1 and/or Scope 2 emissions for the most recently completed fiscal year; each subsequent fiscal year the registrant must add an attestation for an additional fiscal year until the entire period covered by the registrant's GHG disclosures is attested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple GHG emissions attestation providers have provided reports for different fiscal years in a filing, a provider should be clear about its involvement with any historical information and should disclaim involvement where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitable criteria for measurement/evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prevailing attestation standards require the criteria against which the subject matter is measured or evaluated to be 'suitable' — i.e., criteria that, when followed, will result in reasonably consistent measurement/evaluation within the scope of the engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 1505 of Regulation S‑K is intended to satisfy the 'suitable criteria' requirement by setting relevant, objective, measurable, and complete disclosure expectations for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaiming an opinion does not satisfy attestation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A report stating that the GHG emissions attestation provider is disclaiming an opinion on the GHG emissions does not constitute compliance by the AF or LAF with the requirement to obtain an attestation report under the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants required to obtain attestation must obtain a report that provides the required level of assurance/opinion rather than a disclaimer of opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to obtain an attestation over internal control effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules do not require a registrant to obtain an attestation report specifically covering the effectiveness of internal control over GHG emissions disclosure, even where the engagement is performed at a reasonable assurance level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given evolving GHG reporting and assurance practices, initial requirements focus on limited (and later reasonable) assurance over disclosed emissions rather than internal control attestations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider must perform engagement in accordance with chosen attestation standard (including 'other information' requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: A GHG emissions attestation provider must perform the engagement in accordance with the requirements included in the attestation standard being used; if that standard requires the provider to consider 'other information', the provider must comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an attestation standard used by the provider includes requirements to consider other information, the provider's performance of the engagement must reflect those requirements to be in accordance with the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance over consolidated reporting must cover consolidated subsidiaries' information
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated information included in a parent's Commission filing must comply with the final rules applicable to the parent company — meaning subsidiary information that is part of consolidated reporting must be assured as part of assurance over the parent's consolidated reporting, even if the subsidiary itself is not separately subject to assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with how auditing standards apply to consolidated financial statements and may require parent‑level assurance to include subsidiary data used in consolidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of other practitioners' work is constrained by standards (accountant vs non‑accountant)
rubrics_metrics.description: AICPA attestation standards allow a provider performing the Commission‑required assurance to use the work of another accounting practitioner (accountant), but do not address use of the work of a non‑accountant practitioner using different attestation standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, registrants and providers should be mindful of limitations when relying on work performed under different standards or by non‑accountants; Commission staff is available for practice questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant disclosure of oversight inspection program(s) for the engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require a registrant to disclose whether the GHG emissions attestation engagement is subject to any oversight inspection program, and if so, identify which program(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For these purposes, an engagement is 'subject to an oversight inspection program' if it is possible the assurance services could be inspected under the program, even if not certain for a particular cycle (e.g., AICPA peer review). This disclosure is required in the filing containing the attestation report (not necessarily in the attestation report itself).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant disclosure of oversight inspection program(s) that apply to the provider
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to engagement‑level oversight, registrants must disclose whether the GHG emissions attestation provider is subject to any oversight inspection program, and if so, identify which program(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is not limited to oversight programs that inspect GHG engagements; any oversight program that applies to the provider (e.g., for financial audits) must be disclosed to help investors understand provider qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: No registrant disclosure required for provider 'license' or record‑keeping (final decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declined to adopt proposed requirements that registrants disclose (1) whether the attestation provider has a license from any licensing or accreditation body, and (2) whether the provider is subject to record‑keeping requirements for the engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: lack of universal certification/licensure makes determining 'license' status difficult; record‑keeping disclosure would add burden with marginal investor benefit. These items were proposed but not adopted in the final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant disclosure of provider resignation/dismissal and disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 1506(d)(2) requires AFs and LAFs subject to Item 1506(a) to disclose whether their former GHG emissions attestation provider resigned or was dismissed and the date; and if so, whether there were any disagreements during the engagement over measurement, disclosure, or attestation scope, to describe each disagreement and state whether the registrant authorized the former provider to respond fully to successor inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is modeled on Item 4.01 of Form 8‑K and Item 304 of Regulation S‑K, tailored for GHG attestation; it aims to surface significant disagreements that could affect investor assessment of disclosure reliability. The Commission chose to include this disclosure in the filing containing the attestation report to limit burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions/definition for 'disagreements' and communication standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules include two instructions defining the term 'disagreements' for purposes of the resignation/dismissal disclosure and explaining when it is sufficient to conclude a disagreement has been communicated to the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These instructions are consistent with Item 304 and its instructions, with minor modifications for GHG attestation context; registrants should follow these instructions when determining what disagreements to disclose and whether they were communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability limits for resignation/dismissal disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The resignation/dismissal and disagreement disclosure requirement applies only to AFs and LAFs required to obtain an attestation report under Item 1506(a). It does not apply if the AF or LAF is not required to disclose its GHG emissions for a fiscal year (e.g., because emissions are immaterial) and does not apply to registrants that voluntarily obtain assurance and report under Item 1506(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should determine applicability based on mandatory attestation obligations before preparing these disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary assurance disclosure items
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant voluntarily subjects its GHG disclosures to third‑party attestation or verification (Item 1506(e) / proposed Item 1505(e)), the registrant must disclose: (i) identify the provider; (ii) describe the assurance/verification standard used; (iii) describe the level and scope of assurance/verification provided; (iv) briefly describe the results; (v) disclose whether the provider has any other business relationships or professional services with the registrant that may impair independence; and (vi) disclose any oversight inspection program to which the service provider is subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are intended to help investors understand the nature and reliability of voluntary assurance. Commenters suggested additional approaches (e.g., furnishing the report), and there was mixed input on requiring provider independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of disclosure — included in the filing containing GHG disclosures and attestation report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission requires the disclosures described by the final rules to be included in the registration statement or annual report that contains the GHG disclosures and attestation report, rather than in separate filings (e.g., Form 8‑K) or necessarily within the attestation report itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This placement is intended to limit additional filing burden and to ensure investors see the context and related disclosures together. Registrants are expected to obtain the necessary information from providers and will likely already have it when engaging them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of furnishing the attestation/verification report or a link
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposing Release requested comment on whether registrants should be required to furnish a copy of, or provide a link to, the assurance or verification report when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters were split: some favored furnishing the report, others argued that summarizing the report effectively constitutes filing it. The final rules do not mandate furnishing the full report, but registrants and commenters raised it as an option for investor access.
